title: Sunday · the first color
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: The first Sunday. The first watercolor. Over-wet. The Rain, in a color that doesn't know what it's doing yet.

margin.note: The gull, in ink, over a color that bled into it.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the beach in January rain, watercolor. The wash has bled past the ink everywhere. The sky is a puddle. It is, unmistakably, the first time.

image.prompt: a wide beach in January rain as a first attempt at watercolor: the washes bleeding far past the ink lines, the sky a gray puddle, two small figures, over-wet and uncertain, brush-pen ink under it
image.notes: Deliberately over-wet. The book keeps this to show the learning.

panels.name: The beach

panels.composition: Tier 2: the spruce grove. The green has run into the black. A man and a dog at its foot.

image.prompt: a spruce grove in watercolor where the green wash has run into the black ink, a man and a small dog at its foot, over-wet, rain

panels.name: The grove

panels.composition: Tier 3: the two of them from behind, walking back. The color slightly better in this tier than the first, as if he learned during the page.

image.prompt: a man and a dog seen from behind walking down a rainy beach, the watercolor noticeably more controlled than the tiers above it, gray and sea-green washes, no words
image.notes: Improvement within the page. That's the point of keeping it.

panels.name: Back

art.palette: first watercolor: gray, sea-green, everything bleeding

notes: The first Sunday, the first color, the first Rain in watercolor. Kept for the learning.
